In February, 1,897 people registered for the #AfghanEvac global briefing, 781 of them joining from inside Afghanistan. 49 congressional offices were on the call. The practical advice to Afghan allies, delivered plainly: make a life somewhere else.

Veterans and immigrants share more than most people realize. My conversation with @ChamberlainVets founder Chris Purdy changed how I think about both and about my own identity as a veteran doing immigration research.

I'll be honest, this conversation was part interview, part counseling session for me. I haven't always known what to do with my veteran identity in relation to this work. Chris helped me think through it in ways that were meaningful.

The conversation with Chris is on my Substack. Today at 11:30 AM ET, immigration attorney and military law expert Margaret Stock joins me on the legal architecture of veteran deportation and military spouse arrests.

The number of detainees at Delaney Hall, a Newark ICE facility, who signed a letter this week detailing awful conditions inside. 2nd collective grievance letter in 3 months from the same facility.

5

The number of suicides in ICE detention facilities so far in 2026, highest in two decades, with the year not yet half over. 9 total since Trump's 2nd term began. 19 facilities failed ICE's own suicide prevention standards.

$18,000

The proposed new deportation fine per person under a Trump admin rule, up from $5k. DHS has already issued $36B in fines to ~65k people, averaging $553K each. Most expected to go uncollected. The goal isn't revenue, it's self-deportation. Public comment closes June 22.

<60,000

The approximate number of people currently in ICE detention—a figure that is not publicly available. ICE's biweekly data is over a month old. Unverifiable reports say 57,000–58,000. Congress needs to fix the transparency gap.

145,000

The estimated number of U.S. citizen children who have had at least one parent arrested and detained by ICE since January 2025. ICE doesn't report family data. Brookings cross-referenced arrest records with census data to find them. The real number could be higher.

This Week by the {Immigration} Numbers (May 22, 2026)

She believes recovery will require something like a Truth and Reconciliation Commission. "It's going to be a long, long process." That's not a partisan talking point, it's a warning from someone who has testified before Congress for decades.

Stock is also sounding the alarm about what she's seeing in court right now: falsified arrest warrants, false affidavits, clients shipped across the country to evade scrutiny. "The quality of DOJ practice has dropped into the basement."
"To get a green card, you have to qualify for one. To get U.S. citizenship by being born in America, you don't have to have any particular qualifications.": Margaret Stock

For context: only about 2 in 10 Americans currently meet basic military enlistment standards, due to obesity, drug use, and other disqualifying factors. The recruiting pool is shrinking. Immigrants are filling a gap we can't afford to ignore.

Today, immigrant recruits score 20 points higher on the Armed Forces Qualification Test than native-born recruits, have lower dropout rates from basic training, and re-enlist at higher rates. At the Pentagon, Stock calls it a good return on investment.

After 9/11, the U.S. already had intelligence that could have stopped the attacks. It just hadn't been translated. That failure is part of what drove Stock to design the MAVNI program, recruiting noncitizens with critical language and medical skills.

During WWII, German Jewish refugees were naturalized at basic training, sent back to interrogate German POWs, and were responsible for 60% of actionable intelligence on the Western Front. Stock: "You can argue they won the war for the United States."

Stock's argument isn't just that immigration is humane. It's that immigration is strategic. "Immigration was always the secret sauce of the United States," she said. "Without immigration, we were not a superpower."

Army veteran, West Point professor, MacArthur genius grant recipient, and one of the top immigration lawyers in the country, Margaret Stock has a message that every national security hawk needs to hear.🧵
